extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and researchers (editorial offices and editorial staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of COPE guidance documents advising editors, publishers, and researchers on best practices in publication ethics across topics such as peer review, editorial responsibilities, consent, retractions, and misconduct handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics toolkit for a successful editorial office
rubrics_metrics.description: To help ensure the integrity of the scholarly record and the publication process, editorial offices should define and implement best practices in publication ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This COPE guide is a comprehensive toolkit that explains expected ethical practices in scholarly publishing, and highlights resources for editorial offices to develop their codes of ethical conduct and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance advising editors, publishers, and researchers on expected practices and appropriate circumstances regarding the editing of peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines examine the need for journals to amend peer reviews and provide insight into situations where editing peer reviews might be appropriate; journals should have clear policies on when and how reviews may be edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of editorial board appointment and engagement, roles and responsibilities, and recruitment considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides key details to consider during recruitment such as conflicts arising from participation on multiple editorial boards; intended to advise editors and publishers on expected publication ethics practice regarding board membership and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for managing the relationships between society owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on policies and relationships among society-owned journals, the society, and any commercial publisher to ensure ethical publication practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises that policies and relationships must be of the highest quality, ethically sound, and as transparent as possible regardless of publication arrangements or number of affiliated journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint principles developed with DOAJ, OASPA, and WAME describing transparency and best practices for scholarly publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out expected practices (e.g., transparency around editorial processes and business models) that journals and publishers should follow to be considered trustworthy; intended as cross-organisational standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports: guidance from COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles around consent and consent forms for editors to use when developing forms for their journals' purposes relating to medical case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides editors on what constitutes adequate consent for publishing identifiable medical information and offers template considerations for consent forms and policies to safeguard patient privacy and ethical publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of information among editors-in-chief regarding possible misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how EICs can share information about suspected misconduct to preserve the integrity of the scientific record and facilitate investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that sharing information can allow affected journals to conduct investigations with greater efficiency and effectiveness, and outlines considerations for appropriately exchanging such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines intended to advise editors and publishers on expected practice when identifying sections of the same text appearing in more than one of an author's own publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides advice on when text recycling is acceptable or problematic, and suggests editorial actions and policy wording to handle overlapping text across an author's publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to ethical editing for new editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary of the key principles, tasks and relationships of the journal editor role aimed at new editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarises essential duties, common ethical issues, and practical tasks for new editors who may be working without day-to-day contact with editorial colleagues; intended as an introductory primer on ethical editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: research, audit and service evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance regarding what type of study requires ethical approval and how to handle submissions that may not meet a journal’s requirements for independent ethical approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that regulations vary worldwide; offers advice to editors on handling manuscripts reporting research, audits or service evaluations where local approvals differ, to avoid inappropriate rejection due to misunderstanding of local regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic principles and standards to which all peer reviewers should adhere during the peer review process in research publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be applied across disciplines; outlines peer reviewers' ethical obligations, expectations of confidentiality, declarations of competing interests, and standards of conduct while reviewing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the complementary duties of institutions and journals in handling research and publication misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that institutions are responsible for researcher conduct and fostering a healthy environment, while journals are responsible for editors, safeguarding the research record, and ensuring the reliability of published material; provides advice on collaboration during investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for editors on when a retraction should be considered, what to include in a retraction notice, timing, who should issue it, and how to handle cases of inconclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers practical steps and considerations for issuing retractions to correct the literature, including wording and process issues to maintain transparency and protect the integrity of the scholarly record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for governing boards of learned society journals on management and ethical responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises that management should be of the highest quality and ethically sound and provides advice to boards on governance, oversight, and safeguarding editorial independence and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for new researchers on good authorship practice and advice on how to deal with authorship issues as they arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers practical recommendations for establishing authorship criteria, preventing disputes, and resolving conflicts when they occur, targeted at early-career researchers and mentors.
